feature.title: Carotid Stenting Gets a Double Win, Medtronic's RDN Delivers -18.2 mmHg, and AI Hits the Hospital Firewall: MedTech's Big Week
feature.summary: The week of November 10–14, 2026 delivered a cluster of high-impact medtech results spanning cardiovascular devices, AI clinical deployment, wound care, and diagnostics. Two separate carotid stent systems — Contego Medical's Neuroguard IEP Direct and InspireMD's CGuard Prime — earned fresh FDA approvals backed by pivotal trial data showing 0% stroke rates, while Medtronic's SPYRAL AFFIRM post-approval study confirmed an 18.2 mmHg blood pressure reduction for its renal denervation catheter. On the AI front, Dyania Health's hospital-deployed clinical reasoning platform went live inside health system firewalls with NVIDIA infrastructure, and AEYE Health's autonomous diabetic retinopathy screener continued its real-world rollout backed by three pivotal trials exceeding 1,200 patients. The overarching theme is a shift from proof-of-concept to measurable, real-world deployment across cardiology, diagnostics, and AI-assisted care.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: Medtronic's SPYRAL AFFIRM post-approval study confirmed its renal denervation system cut office systolic blood pressure by 18.2 mmHg at six months with no increase in medication — triggering expanded FDA labeling for diabetic and CKD patients.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: Carotid stroke prevention is seeing a hardware arms race: within 48 hours, both Contego Medical (0% stroke rate in PERFORMANCE III) and InspireMD (100% device success in CGUARDIANS II) secured separate FDA approvals for TCAR stent systems, signaling fierce competition in the 35,000+ annual procedure market.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: SeaStar Medical's NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal trial for acute kidney injury in ICU patients has hit 75% enrollment (251/339), with Breakthrough Device Designation for priority FDA review — a readout could reshape critical care nephrology in 2027.

articles.title: Medtronic SPYRAL AFFIRM Post-Approval Study Cuts Office BP 18.2 mmHg; FDA Updates Labeling
articles.snippet: Medtronic's Symplicity Spyral renal denervation system met its primary endpoint in the SPYRAL AFFIRM post-approval study, delivering statistically significant blood pressure reductions across office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory measures at six months in patients with uncontrolled hypertension — with no increase in antihypertensive medications. The FDA simultaneously approved updated labeling to include data for patients with isolated systolic hypertension, chronic kidney disease up to stage 3b, and type 2 diabetes, broadening the therapy's clinical reach.
articles.result: −18.2 mmHg office systolic BP at 6 months, p<0.0001

articles.title: FDA Approves Contego Medical's Neuroguard IEP Direct System for TCAR-IEP After 0% Stroke Rate in Pivotal Trial
articles.snippet: The FDA granted premarket approval (PMA) for Contego Medical's Neuroguard IEP Direct System and 510(k) clearance for its Embolic Protection System, based on the PERFORMANCE III pivotal study in 146 patients across 26 sites, which reported zero strokes, zero MIs, zero neurological deaths, zero cranial nerve injuries, and zero stent thromboses through 30 days. The dual-neuroprotection approach — combining flow reversal and an integrated 40-micron embolic filter — achieves the lowest reported event rates in any prospective multicenter carotid revascularization study.
articles.result: 0% stroke rate, 0.69% MAE rate (ITT) in 146 patients

articles.title: InspireMD's CGuard Prime Wins FDA TCAR Approval on 100% Device Success Rate in CGUARDIANS II Trial
articles.snippet: On November 12, 2026, the FDA approved InspireMD's PMA supplement for the CGuard Prime TransCarotid Stent System for use in TCAR procedures, supported by the prospective, multicenter CGUARDIANS II pivotal trial across 11 US sites, which showed 100% acute device success and no deaths, strokes, MIs, or stent thromboses at 30 days. The approval doubles InspireMD's U.S. addressable market by unlocking access to more than 35,000 annual TCAR procedures, establishing CGuard Prime as the only system offered for both CAS and TCAR delivery.

articles.title: AEYE-DS AI Diabetic Retinopathy Screener Wins 2026 Prix Galien Award; Real-World Clinic Deployment Achieves 95.7% Result Rate
articles.snippet: AEYE Health's FDA-cleared AEYE-DS autonomous AI retinal screener — validated across three prospective pivotal studies in 1,200+ patients with 92–93% sensitivity, 89–94% specificity, and >99% imageability — won the 2026 Prix Galien USA Award for Best Digital Health Solution and is now embedded in ADA clinical guidelines as a named standard-of-care platform. A published real-world implementation study at an endocrinology outpatient clinic found definitive diagnostic results for 95.7% of 256 patients without pharmacological dilation, with over 80% of patients rating the experience as easy, time-efficient, and recommendable.

articles.title: Dyania Health and NVIDIA Deploy Clinical Reasoning AI Inside Hospital Firewalls at Population Scale
articles.snippet: Dyania Health announced on November 13, 2026 a collaboration with NVIDIA to deploy its Synapsis AI clinical reasoning platform inside health system infrastructure — running on NVIDIA TensorRT within the hospital's own private network, eliminating external data exposure. The system processes each patient's full longitudinal chart the way a specialist would, estimating individual cardiovascular risk at 3, 5, and 10 years and updating dynamically with each new imaging result, targeting deployment across entire patient populations rather than isolated workflows.
articles.result: Full hospital-population deployment; on-premises inference operational

articles.title: Google AMIE AI in Primary Care: 114 Real Patients, Zero Safety Stops in Lancet-Published Trial at BIDMC
articles.snippet: A prospective real-world study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center — described as the first of its kind for patient-facing AI in primary care and published in The Lancet — deployed Google's AMIE chatbot to interview 114 patients about symptoms before physician visits, with physician supervision available to halt interactions on four predefined safety triggers. Across 98 analyzed encounters, not one safety stop was triggered, and the AI achieved 90% top-7 diagnosis inclusion, with patient attitudes toward AI improving significantly after the interaction (p<0.001).
articles.result: 0 safety stops across 98 encounters; 90% top-7 diagnosis rate

articles.title: PlaqueTec BIOPATTERN Intracoronary Liquid Biopsy Trial Hits 100 Patients, Expands to 8 NHS Cardiac Centers
articles.snippet: PlaqueTec's BIOPATTERN clinical trial — using its proprietary Liquid Biopsy System to sample blood directly at the site of coronary plaque and identify proteomic biomarkers for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease — recruited its 100th patient and expanded to eight NHS specialist cardiac centers across England. Earlier interim data from the trial's first 33 patients confirmed distinct protein gradients between intracoronary and systemic blood, validating the safety and functionality of the device and supporting the trial's continuation toward its 300-patient target.
articles.result: 100 patients enrolled; expanded to 8 NHS centers; protein gradients confirmed

articles.title: SeaStar Medical NEUTRALIZE-AKI Pivotal Trial Reaches 75% Enrollment; Pediatric QUELIMMUNE Revenue Up 247%
articles.snippet: SeaStar Medical reported that its randomized NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal trial for adult ICU patients with acute kidney injury has enrolled 251 of 339 intended patients (74%), with Breakthrough Device Designation in place enabling priority FDA review upon submission. The company's commercially deployed pediatric therapy QUELIMMUNE — which presented statistically significant higher survival data at ASN Kidney Week 2026 — delivered 247% revenue growth year-over-year, demonstrating early commercial validation of the SCD therapy platform.

articles.title: Bechtel Medical's Wound VOX Earns First FDA 510(k) Clearance for Combined NPWT + Topical Oxygen Wound Therapy
articles.snippet: Bechtel Medical received FDA 510(k) clearance on November 10, 2026 for Wound VOX — the first combined negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) and topical oxygen therapy (TOT) system cleared via the 510(k) pathway — with a limited commercial rollout planned for December 2026. The system offers three therapy modes and is intended to improve outcomes via faster wound closure, reduced infection risk, and improved tissue quality, eliminating the complexity of running two separate wound care device systems simultaneously.
articles.result: First-ever FDA-cleared combined NPWT+TOT system; December launch planned

articles.title: FDA Formally Classifies AI-Based Digital Cervical Cytology Imaging System and MCI Prognostic Software as Class II Devices
articles.source: Alston & Bird Health Care Week in Review
articles.snippet: On November 4, 2026 the FDA issued final classification orders establishing two new AI-enabled diagnostic software categories as Class II medical devices: a Digital Cervical Cytology Slide Imaging System with AI Algorithm for pathology, and Prognostic Assessment Software for Mild Cognitive Impairment for neurology. Both classifications confirm that the agency has determined these AI-driven diagnostics provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness, opening a formal regulatory pathway for commercial deployment across health systems.
articles.result: Two AI diagnostic software categories permanently classified as Class II

articles.title: Hospital AI Sepsis Bundle Compliance Rises from 70.1% to 82.9% in Cluster-Randomized Trial of AI-Assisted Abstraction
articles.snippet: A cluster-randomized trial published in Frontiers in Medicine found that AI-enabled clinical data abstraction and real-time feedback increased compliance with the SEP-1 Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management Bundle from 70.1% to 82.9% — a 13-percentage-point improvement — representing one of the clearest demonstrations of AI driving measurable protocol adherence in critical care. Separately, a stepped-wedge randomized trial in the same review found that in 71,487 study-period notes, AI-generated documentation reduced clinician note time by 0.36 hours per 8 hours of patient care.

articles.title: FDA Clears Wearable Vibration Device for Orthopedic Use as New Class II Category
articles.snippet: The FDA issued a final order on November 4, 2026 formally classifying the Wearable Vibration Device for Orthopedic Use as a Class II medical device, establishing special controls and a codified regulatory pathway for the category. The classification follows clinical evidence supporting wearable sensors in postsurgical orthopedic monitoring, including published data showing 52% better bone stimulus tracking and 371% better impact load monitoring in knee arthroplasty patients compared to standard methods.
articles.result: New Class II device category established; 52% better bone stimulus tracking in validation data
